sample_unit: stakeholders completing structured evaluations (136 AI output safety assessments across 8 scenarios)

links.outcome: Clinician ratings of AI output safety across standardized scenarios
links.effect: 113/136 (83%) AI outputs acceptable as shown; 23/136 (17%) acceptable only with human review; none unacceptable.
links.quote: Overall, 113/136 (83%) AI outputs were rated acceptable as shown, while 23/136 (17%) were considered acceptable only with human review; no AI output was rated unacceptable.

links.outcome: Performance under simulated local use conditions via scenario-based field validation
links.effect: Scenario-based field validation in Sokoto found outputs largely acceptable and identified three improvements needed before pilot.
links.quote: Three operational improvements were identified before pilot implementation: clearer protocols for interpreting distress, refinement of language to minimise potentially stigmatizing expressions, and automatic escalation of suspected psychotic symptoms.

links.outcome: Hausa transcription, translation, and summary generation quality scores
links.effect: Mean 9.9/10 Hausa transcription, 9.9/10 Hausa-to-English translation, 9.2/10 English-to-Hausa summary generation.
links.quote: Mean language quality scores were 9.9/10 for Hausa transcription, 9.9/10 for Hausa-to-English translation, and 9.2/10 for English-to-Hausa summary generation.

unlisted_practices: cultural adaptation of AI mental health screening tool
stakeholder perception of religion and culture as determinants of trust

screen.reason: Empirical scenario-based field validation of an AI system for mental health screening assessing safety, language quality, cultural appropriateness, and workflow readiness with frontline workers, but without testing a specific comparative deployment safeguard.
